ai.title: CLI undo/redo switch to typed commands
ai.summary: Removed `keypress` listener in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` handling `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+R`/`ESC`. Replaced with text input parsing for `undo`/`u`, `redo`/`r`, and `help`/`h`. Updated startup prompt in `npm-app/src/index.ts` and menu text in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to reflect typed commands.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line tool, you no longer undo or redo changes by pressing keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+U or Ctrl+R. Instead, you type plain-text commands: "undo" or "u" to step back, "redo" or "r" to step forward, and "help" or "h" to see the full list of available commands. The on-screen tips and startup message have been updated to show these new instructions, and the old shortcut reminders have been replaced. This change is live today in the command-line version of the tool.

ai.title: Restore ESC to cancel generation in CLI
ai.summary: Added keypress listener in npm-app/src/cli.ts to handle 'escape' key, invoking handleEscKey() to stop response generation. Removed fallback menu display logic from handleEscKey(), ensuring ESC strictly cancels active generation without side effects.

eli5.text: People using the command-line tool can press the Escape key again to stop the assistant from generating a response mid-sentence, just like it worked before. The program now listens for that key press and immediately halts the ongoing reply instead of showing a menu or doing something else. This affects anyone interacting with the assistant through the terminal, and the change was released today as part of the latest version.

ai.title: CLI menu layout and tips updated
ai.summary: CLI menu groups commands under COMMANDS header with bullet prefixes. Tips section replaces static knowledge.md guidance with prompts to generate knowledge files and handle corrections. lastInputWasMenu state removed from CLI class. Changes confined to npm-app/src/cli.ts and npm-app/src/menu.ts.

eli5.text: When you open the in-app help menu, the command list now appears under a clear 'COMMANDS' heading with bullet points, making it easier to scan. The tips section no longer suggests creating a general knowledge.md file; instead, it prompts you to ask the assistant to generate project-specific knowledge files and reminds you to update them when the assistant makes mistakes. A small bit of internal tracking that remembered whether your last action came from the menu has been removed, but this doesn't change what you see or do.

ai.title: Fix CLI undo/redo status messages
ai.summary: Moved undo/redo console logs in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to execute only after successful version navigation, adding explicit 'No more undo/redo' feedback on failure. Updated `npm-app/src/menu.ts` help text to standardize bullet formatting for the 'Don't change any files' tip. Scope limited to CLI interaction surfaces.

eli5.text: When you use undo or redo in the command-line version, the message about what you're doing now appears only after the switch actually succeeds, and you'll see a clear notice if there's nothing left to undo or redo. The helper tips shown in the command-line menu were also tweaked for consistent formatting, making the instructions easier to scan.

ai.title: Suppress meta-comments in diff generation
ai.summary: Added instruction to `generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts` to omit meta-comments like "Add this import" from output. Updated examples to include such comments, demonstrating the exclusion rule. Ensures cleaner diffs by removing noise.

eli5.text: When the system prepares updates for your code, it now automatically removes placeholder comments like "// Add this import" that were only meant to explain the change. This affects anyone who reviews or applies the generated updates, since the diffs will no longer contain these distracting annotations. If you looked at the output today, you'd see cleaner, more focused changes without the extra commentary cluttering the view.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.42
ai.summary: Incremented version field to 1.0.42 in backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Internal release bump.

eli5.text: Today the assistant quietly moved up to a new release number for the version that ships the internal tools and the command-line helper. This is the kind of change that happens behind the scenes to mark a new build, so if you looked for it you might only see the current version shown somewhere in the app, and you wouldn't notice anything working differently. Nothing about what the assistant does or what you can sign up for changed today, so if you're a user you can keep using it exactly as before.

ai.title: CLI auto-stages changes via git add .
ai.summary: CLI `stageChanges` helper executes `git add .` via `child_process.exec` before `sendUserInputAndAwaitResponse`. Ensures working tree state is captured prior to agent processing. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Error handling silently swallows `exec` failures.

eli5.text: When you send a message to the assistant in the command-line tool, it now quietly saves the current state of your project files before processing what you typed. This only affects people using the command-line version of the tool, and you wouldn't see anything happen on screen. The change silently fixes issues in the background if something goes wrong while saving, with no notifications or error messages.

ai.title: Add hallucinated patch test case
ai.summary: Adds `hallucinated` mock data and test case for `generatePatch`. Verifies streaming response handling and file block processing logic. Covers backend test suite only.

eli5.text: The software's testing system now includes a new practice scenario that mimics how it handles messy, incomplete, or incorrect responses from the AI assistant. This helps the team catch problems before they reach you, but it doesn't change what you experience directly. If you've noticed the assistant occasionally stumbles when processing complex file changes, this update strengthens the behind-the-scenes checks to improve reliability over time.

ai.title: Stronger updatefilecontext prompt
ai.summary: The system prompt now explicitly directs the agent to verify completeness of the <relevant_files> block before proceeding. This change strengthens the instruction to use update_file_context when needed files are missing, while retaining the constraint against requesting files absent from <project_file_tree>. The modification is isolated to backend/src/system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: When the coding assistant reviews your code, it now more clearly checks that it already has every file it needs listed in the relevant_files block before continuing, and will only request additional files that actually exist in the project. In practice you may notice the assistant pauses to ask you to provide a missing file rather than silently working with an incomplete picture, but it won't keep asking for files that aren't part of your project. This is a small behind-the-scenes tightening of the assistant's instructions that affects anyone having the assistant review their code.

ai.title: Improve error handling in diff generation and CLI
ai.summary: Refactored `generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts` to log errors and return `oldContent` instead of throwing on extraction failures. Updated `main-prompt.ts` to catch `processFileBlock` errors, log them, and filter empty results from the final changes array. Tweaked `cli.ts` to print a newline after stopping the loading animation and adjusted `menu.ts` prompt instructions.

eli5.text: When the program runs into a problem reading or changing a file, it will now skip past that file and keep working instead of stopping everything and showing an error message. If you were using the command-line tool, you will no longer see a jarring blank line after the loading spinner stops; a newline is printed automatically so the next output appears cleanly. The text shown in the command-line menu was also reworded slightly to make a prompt tip clearer. These are behind-the-scenes stability fixes for people running the tool from a terminal.

ai.title: stageChanges cd project root
ai.summary: stageChanges in npm-app/src/cli.ts now prefixes git add . with cd ${getProjectRoot()}. Import of getProjectRoot added from project-files. Ensures staging runs against correct directory regardless of current working directory.

eli5.text: The program now makes sure it runs the 'save my work' command from the main project folder, instead of whatever folder you happened to be in. This means your work is always saved to the right place, even if you were in a different subfolder when you asked it to save. This only affects a behind-the-scenes tool used by people building the program, not the program's regular features.
